props.title: License to Wed

sections.content: **License to Wed** (2007) represents one of the more misguided attempts at wedding-themed comedy, following in the footsteps of far superior films like **Father of the Bride** (1991) and **My Big Fat Greek Wedding** (2002). Robin Williams plays an intrusive minister who forces engaged couple Ben (John Krasinski) and Sadie (Mandy Moore) through an extreme marriage preparation course. The film stumbles where classics like **The Philadelphia Story** (1940) soared, turning what could have been clever commentary on modern relationships into awkward slapstick and uncomfortable scenarios.

sections.content: The wedding comedy genre hit its stride in the late 1990s with gems like **My Best Friend's Wedding** (1997) and **The Wedding Singer** (1998), which balanced romance with genuine character development. These films succeeded by grounding their humor in relatable relationship dynamics rather than contrived situations. **License to Wed** unfortunately follows the path of lesser entries like **You, Me and Dupree** (2006) and **Just Married** (2003), relying on manufactured conflict and broad comedy that undermines its central romance.

Robin Williams, who brought warmth and humanity to roles in films like **Mrs. Doubtfire** (1993) and **Good Will Hunting** (1997), feels wasted here in a character that comes across as more creepy than comedic. The film sits awkwardly among other religious-themed romantic comedies like **Keeping the Faith** (2000) and **Leap of Faith** (1992), but lacks their thoughtful exploration of faith and relationships. sections.content: By the late 2000s, wedding comedies had largely exhausted their traditional formulas, leading to more subversive takes like **Wedding Crashers** (2005) and **Bridesmaids** (2011). **License to Wed** arrived at this transitional moment but failed to innovate, instead falling back on tired tropes and dated humor. The film's failure highlighted the need for fresh approaches to the genre, which later arrived with films like **Crazy Rich Asians** (2018) and **Palm Springs** (2020).
